title: Contract Compliance
summary: Share of spend following negotiated terms and approved channels.
whyPeCares: PE cares because this KPI gives an early read on growth quality, margin expansion, cash conversion, execution discipline, or exit-story credibility.
goodBadSignals: Good performance shows controlled execution and improving unit economics; bad performance signals leakage, weak process ownership, or a diligence risk requiring deeper segmentation.

articleSections.title: Strategic Context & Value Driver
body: In the wake of a private equity acquisition, contract compliance is the critical mechanism that ensures 'paper savings' negotiated during the RFP process actually manifest as 'realized savings' in the P&L. We find that mid-market companies often suffer from a 15-25% 'Compliance Gap'—where goods and services are purchased outside of negotiated terms due to poor oversight or vendor invoicing errors. For an Operating Partner, closing this gap is a foundational step in institutionalizing financial discipline and protecting the investment's underwritten margins.

Contract compliance is more than just a procurement metric; it is a direct reflection of a company's internal control environment. Failure to monitor compliance leads to 'Revenue Leakage' for the company and 'Margin Erosion' for the GP, effectively subsidizing the vendor's profit at the expense of the fund's returns. By establishing a rigorous compliance framework, we ensure that every dollar of spend is aligned with the Value Creation Plan (VCP) and that the company is fully capturing the volume incentives and rebates it has earned.

The strategic driver here is the professionalization of the vendor relationship. A business that lacks compliance monitoring is often viewed by vendors as an easy target for 'price creep' and unapproved surcharges. By demonstrating that we are tracking compliance at a granular level, we reset the power dynamic in favor of the portfolio company, ensuring that the vendor remains a high-performing partner rather than a source of hidden costs. This discipline is essential for scaling the business and preparing it for a rigorous exit process.
articleSections.callout: Negotiated savings are meaningless if they never hit the P&L—contract compliance is the bridge from 'Paper' to 'Bank'.

articleSections.title: Operational Levers & Benchmarking
body: The primary operational lever for driving contract compliance is the implementation of a 'Three-Way Match' process—aligning the purchase order (PO), the receiving document, and the vendor invoice. We benchmark compliance rates against a 'Best-in-Class' standard of >95% for core categories. Any persistent deviation from this benchmark triggers a root-cause analysis, where we identify whether the non-compliance is due to internal 'Maverick Spend' or vendor-side billing inaccuracies that require immediate remediation.

We also utilize 'Price-Point Audits' to verify that the rates charged on invoices match the master service agreement (MSA) or the most recent pricing addendum. In a high-inflation environment, vendors often implement 'blanket' price increases that bypass negotiated caps or fixed-term agreements. By deploying a systematic audit cadence, the Operating Partner can identify these unauthorized increases and claw back overpayments, often yielding a 2-4% reduction in total category spend without any change in volume or vendor.

Benchmarking also extends to service-level agreement (SLA) compliance, ensuring that vendors are meeting their performance obligations such as on-time delivery or uptime. We install 'Performance Dashboards' that track vendor output against contractually mandated KPIs, allowing us to enforce penalty clauses or negotiate 'service credits' when standards are not met. This operational rigor ensures that the company is receiving the full value of the services it is paying for, directly supporting the broader operational efficiency of the portfolio company.

articleSections.title: Math & Unit Economics (Example Injection)
body: Consider a $300M revenue portfolio company with $120M in addressable indirect spend. A procurement workstream successfully negotiates a 10% reduction in pricing across key categories like shipping, IT services, and facilities, which should theoretically result in $12M of annual EBITDA savings. However, without a compliance monitoring function, we often find that the 'actual' savings realized in the first six months are only 60% of the target, or $7.2M, due to a mix of maverick buying and vendor billing errors.

By investing in a contract compliance audit, we identify $4.8M in 'leaked' savings. For example, if $40M of that spend was on IT services with a 5% billing error rate (e.g., being charged for decommissioned licenses or at old rates), identifying and fixing this single leak adds $2M back to the bottom line immediately. The math is simple: the 'Return on Compliance' (ROC) in this scenario is massive—spending $150k on a specialized audit firm or compliance tool yields a 32x return in found EBITDA that was previously being lost to administrative friction.

On an enterprise value basis, that $4.8M of leaked savings is worth $57.6M at a 12x exit multiple. If the GP fails to capture this compliance delta, they are effectively leaving nearly $60M of EV on the table for the next buyer to capture. This illustration highlights why Operating Partners treat contract compliance as a non-negotiable part of the 'Management Operating Cadence,' as it represents one of the most cost-effective ways to drive value throughout the hold period.

articleSections.title: Technology & Tooling Stack
body: To manage contract compliance at scale, we deploy a 'Contract Lifecycle Management' (CLM) platform such as Ironclad, Icertis, or Conga. These tools act as a centralized 'Single Source of Truth' for all commercial agreements, using AI to extract key metadata such as pricing tables, rebate tiers, and expiration dates. This structured data allows the finance and procurement teams to automate the comparison between invoice data and contract terms, flagging discrepancies in real-time before payments are disbursed.

For spend-side compliance, we integrate the CLM with a 'Procure-to-Pay' (P2P) system like Coupa or GEP Smart. These platforms enforce 'Guided Buying'—directing employees to approved vendors and automatically applying contractually negotiated pricing at the point of purchase. By digitizing the 'Requisition-to-Payment' workflow, we create a transparent audit trail that virtually eliminates maverick spend and ensures that the company is always buying on the most favorable terms available under the master agreement.

In more complex categories like logistics or multi-site facilities management, we utilize 'Audit and Recovery' specialists supported by proprietary data-mining tools like PRGX or Cotiviti. These tools scan millions of historical transactions to identify duplicate payments, missed discounts, and unearned rebates that are often missed by standard ERP reconciliations. This combination of preventative software and retrospective auditing creates a 'Defense-in-Depth' strategy that protects the company's margins from both internal process failures and vendor-side errors.

articleSections.title: Exit Readiness & Multiple Expansion
body: During the exit process, a robust contract compliance program is a powerful signal of 'Operational Excellence' and management discipline. Prospective buyers, particularly strategic ones, will scrutinize the company's vendor contracts and payment history to ensure that the reported EBITDA is 'clean' and sustainable. By presenting a documented track record of compliance monitoring, we provide the buyer with the assurance that the company's margins are not inflated by one-time gains and are protected by durable commercial agreements.

We often include a 'Compliance Audit Certificate' in the vendor management section of the data room, proving that the company has undergone regular third-party reviews of its top vendor relationships. This level of transparency reduces the 'Due Diligence Risk' for the buyer, potentially accelerating the transaction timeline and supporting a premium multiple. It demonstrates that the business has a 'Self-Healing' procurement function that can identify and correct errors without constant GP intervention, making it a highly attractive and lower-risk asset.

Ultimately, contract compliance contributes to multiple expansion by de-risking the 'Cost-Side' of the P&L. A business that can prove it consistently captures its negotiated savings is seen as having more 'Predictable Earnings' than one that is subject to unmanaged price volatility. By institutionalizing compliance as a core business process, we ensure that the value created during the hold period is fully recognized at exit, maximizing the IRR for the fund and cementing the Operating Partner's reputation as a world-class value creator.
